title: Immutable quantized fanout & operator evacuation architecture
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document describes an immutable, operator-driven reference architecture for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments that: (1) hosts quantized model variants, (2) performs controlled fanout to heterogenous GPU pools, and (3) includes an operator evacuation/escape-hatch pattern for rapid rollback or tenant quarantine. The pattern prioritizes reproducible artifacts, minimal runtime drift, and forensic-friendly rollback for regulated customers.

Goals and scope:
- Provide a repeatable topology for customers that need low-latency fanout across heterogeneous accelerators while preserving the ability to safely evacuate traffic and forensically preserve evidence.
- Include deployment packaging constraints, day-2 operator runbook items, upgrade & rollback steps, and a customer readiness checklist.
- Target platforms: VPC-hosted private control plane and fully air-gapped on-prem installs. This reference covers operator-driven, Kubernetes-based deployments with optional lightweight edge gateways.

High-level architecture overview:
- Immutable operator: an operator (redwood-operator) reconciles desired state from signed artifacts. Operators do not modify in-place model binaries — they reference immutable model artifact tags (SHA256) and image digests.
- Quantized model bundles: model artifact bundle contains model weights (quantized formats: int8/4bit) + metadata manifest (architecture version, quantization profile, compatible kernel list).
- Fanout fabric: request routing uses a local routing fabric that supports tiered fallback: local GPU pool -> regional GPU pool -> CPU-safe quantized variant. Routing decisions are policy-driven and annotated in the operator custom resource (CR).
- Evacuation/escape hatch: an operator-run evacuation job that: (a) atomically flips routing policy to safe-mode, (b) snapshots KV cache and in-flight sessions, (c) seals artifacts for forensic export.

Components and ownership:
- redwood-operator (owner: ops/runtime) — reconciles tenants, model bundles, routing CRs, and evacuation jobs.
- runtime-pool (owner: infra/serving-runtime) — per-pool daemonset/statefulset serving quantized bundles.
- routing-proxy (owner: infra/networking) — local gRPC/HTTP proxy that implements policy routing & backpressure.
- telemetry-gateway (owner: observability) — aggregates traces, token-level cost, and sampling for forensic snapshots.

SLOs and operational targets (recommended):
- Availability: 99.95% per-tenant for dedicated pools (business SLA maps to this).
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms for typical 128-token responses on A100/RTX models with quantization profile Q4.
- Evacuation window: operator can place tenant into safe-mode within 30s of triggering evacuation job; full KV snapshot completed within 5 minutes for typical tenant sizes.

Hardware and network requirements (table):
| Component | Minimum | Recommended |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPU type | 1x A10 / T4 equivalent per 4 vcores | A100 / H100 families for high throughput |
| GPU memory | 24 GB | 40+ GB per GPU for large models |
| Node CPU | 8 vCPU | 32 vCPU |
| Node disk | 100GB | 500GB NVMe local cache |
| NIC | 1 Gbps | 25 Gbps RDMA for cross-rack fanout |
| Control plane bandwidth | N/A | 100 Mbps stable to customer control plane 

Packaging & artifact requirements (on-prem constraints):
- All images and model bundles must be signed (cosign) and versioned by digest. Operator requires a signed bundle manifest: {artifact_sha256, quant_profile, compat_kernels}.
- Offline airgap: provide an artifact bundle tarball with: OCI images (gzipped tar), model bundles, operator helm chart, and a verification manifest.
- Image layout: use immutable tags (digest-only in CRs). No floating tags permitted for production private-deploys.

Routing & fanout policy examples (CR snippets expressed as text):
1) Priority-based fanout:
- primary_pool: local-gpu-pool
- fallback_pools: [regional-gpu-pool, cpu-quant-safe]
- latency_target_ms: 200

2) Cost-aware fanout (billing-tier annotation):
- prefer_pool_when: {unit_cost_per_token < 0.0008}
- throttle_on_cost_delta: 2x expected

Day-2 operator runbook (quick actions):
1) Verify operator health:
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood-operator
- Expected: 1/1 READY, restart_count < 3 in 24h

2) Trigger evacuation (safe-mode) for tenant "acme-tenant":
1. redwoodctl tenant safe-mode --tenant acme-tenant --reason "suspected data leak"
2. Operator flips routing CR to safe-mode and returns a job id: evac-20260118-42
3. Monitor snapshot progress: redwoodctl evac status --id evac-20260118-42
4. If snapshot fails, run diagnostic dump: redwoodctl evac dump --id evac-20260118-42 --include-kv --timeout 600

3) Rapid rollback of a model bundle (operator recommended):
1. Pin the previous model digest: kubectl patch modelbundle model-xyz --patch '{"spec":{"artifactDigest":"sha256:old"}}' --type=merge
2. Wait for operator to reconcile and for all runtime-pool replicas to report modelVersion=old in /metrics
3. Run health checks: curl -f http://{proxy}/health/tenant/acme-tenant/ready || rollback-operator-alert

Upgrade procedure (immutable-operator approach):
- Principle: staged artifact promotion using immutable digests, canary traffic split, and operator-ensured rollback.
- Pre-upgrade checks:
  - Ensure signed manifest present for new artifacts and documented kernel compatibility in the CR.
  - Run offline validation suite against synthetic load for cold-starts and KV cache seeding.
- Canary rollout steps:
  1. Create a modelbundle CR referencing new artifact digest and set trafficSplit: 5% to canary_pool.
  2. Monitor p50/p95 latency, error-rate, and token-accuracy regression alerts for 2h.
  3. If stable, increase to 25% for 1h, then 50%, then full promotion.
- Failure/rollback criteria:
  - Error-rate > 1% over baseline 15m window
  - Token-level quality regression > configured threshold (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE fall beyond pre-approved delta)
  - Operator automatically flips canary to safe-mode and reverts trafficSplit to previous digest.

Forensic-friendly rollback & evidence preservation:
- On any operator-triggered rollback, operator will: (a) create an evidence bundle (compressed, signed) containing: routing CR snapshot, modelbundle manifests, KV cache snapshot metadata (and optionally sampled keys), and request traces for the prior 30 minutes.
- Evidence retention: default 90 days for regulated tenants; configurable via tenant manifest.

Customer readiness checklist (pre-install to signoff):
1) Network: required outbound control-plane connectivity for signed manifest verification (unless airgapped).
2) Hardware: node + GPU minimums satisfied and local NVMe cache present.
3) Security: KMS integration for image signing; HSM recommended for private-managed customers.
4) Observability: telemetry-gateway endpoints reachable and sampling set to >= 10% request traces for first 72h after onboarding.
5) Runbook acceptance: customer has validated operator evacuation playbook in a rehearsal drill (see "Evacuation rehearsal template" below).

Evacuation rehearsal template (operator exercise):
1. Schedule a 90-minute game day off-peak.
2. Trigger a tenant-safe-mode for a non-production tenant. Verify routing flips within 30s.
3. Validate KV snapshot completes and is exported to a secure bucket.
4. Reconstitute the tenant into a test cluster from the evidence bundle and compare outputs to pre-evacuation baseline.

Monitoring & telemetry policy recommendations:
- Token-level metrics: collect tokens/second, median token latency, and per-route cost.
- Trace sampling: 10% baseline, 100% for canary periods and evacuation windows.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes -> P1 alert to oncall
  - model mismatch/regression alert (eval harness) -> P1 and automated canary rollback

Known failure modes and mitigations:
- Cold-start latency spikes: mitigate with warmstart pre-warming jobs controlled by operator, and with local NVMe warm caches.
- Incompatible quantization kernels: operator rejects modelbundle if kernel list mismatch; fallback to CPU-safe quantized variant is enabled by default.
- Snapshot failure during evacuation: operator attempts three retries with exponential backoff; if still failing, escalate to field operator for manual snapshot via kubectl exec into runtime-pod.

Operational runbook appendix (commands & examples):
- Inspect modelbundle: kubectl describe modelbundle model-xyz -n redwood
- Force reconcile: kubectl annotate modelbundle model-xyz redwood/reconcile-now=true
- Evacuation status: redwoodctl evac status --id evac-20260118-42 --json
